infoModalDescription: Learn about light pollution, its effects, and how to contribute to a darker night sky
pollutionIntro: Light pollution is the alteration of natural nighttime light levels caused by artificial light sources. This phenomenon has significant consequences for human health, biodiversity, and our ability to observe the night sky.
pollutionHealthText: Exposure to artificial light at night can disrupt circadian rhythms, affecting melatonin production and increasing the risk of sleep disorders, obesity, diabetes, depression, and certain types of cancer.
pollutionHealthRefs: References: Stevens et al. (2014) "Light at night, circadian disruption and breast cancer" British Journal of Cancer; Fonken & Nelson (2014) "The effects of light at night on circadian clocks and metabolism" Endocrine Reviews
pollutionBiodiversityText: Artificial light at night alters navigation, feeding, and reproduction behaviors of many species. It especially affects nocturnal insects, migratory birds, bats, and sea turtles, contributing to biodiversity loss.
pollutionBiodiversityRefs: References: Longcore & Rich (2004) "Ecological light pollution" Frontiers in Ecology; Gaston et al. (2013) "The ecological impacts of nighttime light pollution" Journal of Ecology
pollutionNightSkyText: More than 80% of the world's population lives under light-polluted skies. This loss of the starry sky disconnects us from our natural and cultural heritage, limiting astronomical research and the inspiration that the cosmos has provided to humanity for millennia.
pollutionNightSkyRefs: References: Falchi et al. (2016) "The new world atlas of artificial night sky brightness" Science Advances; Kyba et al. (2017) "Artificially lit surface of Earth at night increasing in radiance and extent" Science Advances
lightingIntro: Well-designed lighting can provide safety and functionality while minimizing light pollution.
lightingColorText:
• Prefer warm lights: Color temperatures below 3000K (amber/yellow tones)
• Avoid blue light: Cool white light (>4000K) suppresses melatonin more and scatters more light in the atmosphere
• Amber LEDs: Best option for outdoor use (1800-2200K)
lightingOrientationText:
• Light downward: Use fully shielded fixtures that direct light only where needed
• Zero upward emission: No light should be emitted above the horizontal
• Avoid glare: Shield light sources so they are not directly visible
lightingIntensityText:
• Only what's needed: Use the minimum intensity that serves the purpose
• Don't over-light: More light doesn't always mean more safety
• Smart dimming: Reduce intensity during low-use hours
lightingDetectionText:
• Motion sensors: Light only when needed
• Timers: Automatic shutdown after required hours
• Energy savings: Reduces consumption and CO₂ emissions
appTitle: How to use the ALAN app
appCaptureText:
• Click the camera button (bottom-right corner)
• Upload a photo of a light pollution source
• Rate the lighting quality from 1 to 5 stars
• Add a description explaining what you see in the image
appMapText:
• Navigate the map to see other users' observations
• Color code: Green (good lighting), Yellow (acceptable), Orange (poor), Red (very poor)
• Click on a marker to see observation details
appCollaborateText:
• You can rate other users' observations
• Together we accurately quantify the degree of light pollution
• Your ratings help create a global map of light pollution from Earth
appSettingsText:
• Access your profile from the top-right menu
• Customize your language and theme preferences
creditsAboutText: ALAN (Artificial Light At Night) is a citizen science platform dedicated to documenting and combating light pollution globally. Our goal is to empower communities with data to promote more sustainable lighting policies.
creditsDevelopmentText: This application has been developed by Alejandro Catalá Espí using modern web technologies including Next.js, React, and Firebase, with the aim of making citizen science accessible to everyone.
